name: Unchecked Sentinel Corrupts a Shared Record
essence: A 'not found' sentinel return used unchecked as a write offset writes past the start of a shared file -- the same unchecked-return defect that elsewhere becomes the CWE-690 null dereference.

examples.summary: ctypes applies the unchecked -1 sentinel before the mapped records buffer, overwriting the preceding file header and persisting the corruption..
examples.mechanism: ctypes applies the unchecked -1 sentinel before the mapped records buffer, overwriting the preceding file header and persisting the corruption.
examples.expected_behavior: Leave catalog HABC intact when Q is absent.

ingredients.suggests: The caller uses the not-found return directly as a write offset.
The pointer references a shared file mapping and the write persists in its header.

examples.summary: An unchecked missing index writes before the mapped record region and permanently changes the file header.
examples.mechanism: unsafe pointer arithmetic applies a negative sentinel to a mapped record subregion, writing before that region into the adjacent file header; this is an actual out-of-bounds subobject write.

ingredients.suggests: The missing lookup sentinel is used as a pointer offset without checking it.
The raw write changes a shared file mapping and a later read observes it.

examples.summary: An unchecked negative record index overwrites the page header and persists it.
examples.mechanism: unsafe pointer offset bypasses bounds and writes before the records subobject into its adjacent header. The missing-record sentinel is used directly as a record offset. The corrupted record page is written back across the persistent file boundary.

ingredients.suggests: The missing-record sentinel is used directly as a record offset.
The corrupted record page is written back across the persistent file boundary.
